images.filename: Magnificent Architecture of the Cathedral of the Madeleine.jpg
images.caption: The Cathedral of the Madeleine is a Roman Catholic church in Salt Lake City, Utah, United States. It was completed in 1909 and currently serves as the cathedral, or mother church, of the Diocese of Salt Lake City. It is the only cathedral in the U.S. under the patronage of St. Mary Magdalene.

It was completed in 1909 and currently serves as the cathedral, or mother church, of the Diocese of Salt Lake City. It is the only cathedral in the U.S. under the patronage of St. Mary Magdalene.

images.filename: 1st Glorious Mystery Stained Glass Window (Resurrection) Cathedral of the Madeleine Salt Lake City.jpg
images.caption: The east transept window at the Cathedral of the Madeline in Salt Lake City was installed in 1908 by F. X. Zettler of the House of Littler, Royal Bavarian Institute in Munich. It is the first in a set of five windows depicting the Glorious Mysteries of the Rosary along the east side of the Cathedral. The window also depicts various saints clockwise from the top: Saint Francis de Sales, Saint Agnes of Rome, Saint Stephen, Saint Ignatius of Loyola, Saint Francis of Assisi, Saint Bernard of Clairvaux, Saint Vincent de Paul, and Saint Monica.

images.filename: 5th Joyful Mystery Window (The Finding of Jesus) Cathedral of the Madeleine Salt Lake City 01.jpg
images.caption: The Finding of Jesus in the Temple Stained Glass Window at the Cathedral of the Madeleine in Salt Lake City was installed in 1908 by F. X. Zettler of the House of Littler, Royal Bavarian Institute in Munich. It is the fifth in a set of five windows depicting the Joyful Mysteries of the Rosary along the west side of the Cathedral. The window includes images of the four gospel writers and selected church fathers (clockwise from the top): St. Gregory, St. Matthew, St. Jerome, St. Mark, St. Augustine, St. Luke, St. Ambrose, and St. John. The window is a gift of Mrs. Mary Judge (1849-1908), widow of John Judge, an Irish immigrant who amassed a fortune at the Silver King Mine in Park City. After John's death in 1892, Mary took over the business and invested heavily in real estate. She built the Judge Building in Salt Lake City in 1908.
